stem: A young child has persistent fever plus bilateral nonexudative conjunctival injection, a polymorphous rash, erythematous swollen hands and feet, and a strawberry tongue. Which condition should the nurse suspect?

options.B: An uncomplicated viral upper respiratory infection.
options.C: A benign medication rash that fully explains all findings.
options.D: A normal childhood variation requiring no evaluation.

rationale: The 2024 American Heart Association scientific statement describes Kawasaki disease as a clinical diagnosis characterized by fever with findings that can include bilateral nonexudative conjunctival injection, rash, swelling and erythema of the hands and feet, and oropharyngeal changes such as strawberry tongue. Early diagnosis matters because untreated disease can lead to coronary artery dilation or aneurysms. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize the classic mucocutaneous clinical pattern of Kawasaki disease and its coronary complication risk.
source_document_title: Update on Diagnosis and Management of Kawasaki Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
source_locator: Diagnosis section and Key Points — fever, nonexudative conjunctival injection, rash, extremity changes, oropharyngeal findings; coronary artery dilation/aneurysm risk
source_claim_supported: Kawasaki disease is a clinical diagnosis characterized by fever and principal mucocutaneous findings including nonexudative conjunctival injection, rash, extremity changes and strawberry tongue; untreated disease can cause coronary dilation or aneurysms.
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation — pediatric systemic/cardiovascular disorders and complication recognition
correction_summary: Upgraded the authority from an older NCBI summary to the current 2024 AHA scientific statement. Removed the obsolete rigid '5+ days required in every complete case' phrasing because the AHA notes complete KD can be diagnosed with four days of fever when at least four principal features are present. Reduced difficulty from hard to easy.
audit_findings: The 2024 AHA update directly supports A and confirms diagnostic criteria did not require the original item's rigid 5-day formulation in all complete cases. B-D cannot explain the full characteristic pattern. Independent second pass passed.
